body:
I need drafted dialogue for three short scenes between Izek Strazni and Ireena Kolyana, brother and sister who do not remember each other (she was found on a road as a girl; he lost her to wolves in the woods when he was nine). Reply with the nodes below only, in the order given, no commentary.

# Part B: three scenes between them

They happen with the party present, at Ireena's door in the place she shelters, or around a camp fire on the road. The party is a group of adventurers the player controls; in each scene the party can say one of two things and Izek and Ireena answer. Each scene is played once, in order.

Each scene's shape: a node named for the scene: Narrator x1, Izek x2, Ireena x2, then two party option rows; then two reply nodes `<scene>_a` and `<scene>_b` (Izek and/or Ireena, x2 lines each). The scene ends after the reply (do not write `-> END`).

~ sister_1: THE DOLL. Izek takes from inside his coat the first doll the toymaker Blinsky ever carved for him, a small wooden woman with red paint for hair, and holds it out. She turns it in her hands. It looks nothing like her (her dry joke), and still she does not give it back. Options: "(Say nothing. Let them have this.)" / "Tell Izek she would like to keep it."
~ sister_2: THE PARENTS. Ireena asks what their parents were like. He has very little to give: a hearth, smoke, a voice calling them in at dusk, a pair of hands. He does not name them. She says it is more than she had this morning. Options: "Tell her the little he has is enough to begin." / "Ask Izek what they were doing in the woods."
~ sister_3: THE NAME. Izek tells her the name he shouted through the trees that night. The name is VIORELA. She says it back once, carefully, like a word in another language. It sounds like a name for someone else; someone braver, maybe. Options: "It is yours to keep or to leave, Ireena." / "You can carry both names." The replies decide which name she keeps: sister_3_a (she keeps Ireena: she asks him to call her that, but says she is glad he told her), and sister_3_b (she keeps both: Ireena by day, and the other when it is he who says it). Name the reply nodes `sister_3_a` and `sister_3_b`.

Count: about 27 lines. Keep Izek flat and short; Ireena dry and exact, never begging, never remembering; nobody cries.

## The game and the format

This is dialogue for a single-player D&D Curse of Strahd game. Plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables), nodes under `~ name`, one line per row as `Speaker [mood]: Text`, party option rows as `* option text -> node_name` (the player's character speaks, first person, short, under 14 words, no skill checks), ASCII only (straight quotes and apostrophes, no accents or fancy dashes, no em-dash: use a comma or a full stop), 1-2 sentences a line, nothing over about 28 words, no placeholders like {name}. Moods allowed: [smile], [angry], [afraid], [sad], [sly], [weary]; most lines carry none. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## Who they are

IZEK STRAZNI: a big, scarred man who was the Baron of Vallaki's enforcer. His right arm is not his own: scaled red-black to the shoulder, clawed, hot to the touch, able to burst into flame. When he was nine, wolves came out of the trees by the lake and took his little sister and his arm; he woke with this one. He has dreamed of a red-haired woman every night since and paid the toymaker Blinsky to carve her face into dolls, a chest of them at the foot of his bed. The party has now told him that the woman is Ireena Kolyana, his lost sister (found wandering on a road as a girl, no memory, raised by the burgomaster Kolyan of Barovia). He believed it. He walked out of the Baron's service ("I won't break any more heads for that fat fool in the sash. I'm done."). He talks to the dolls at night (his secret; he does not say so). How he talks: short, flat, imperatives and threats; never more than two sentences unless about her; about her he goes quiet and almost gentle, which is worse; calls the Baron "my lord" and later "that fat fool". Pet phrases: "Stand back from the Baron." "Not here." "I'm good at waiting." He never says Strahd's name: "him", "the rider", "the castle". He is not funny; the humour is around him. Moods: [angry], [sad] or none.
Some of his existing lines, so you hear him (do NOT repeat them): "You're in my room." / "Good. I've wanted to since the gate." / "She's real. I dream her every night. Her face, her hair." / "I've seen you. Every night since I was nine years old. I didn't know your name. Now I do." / "My sister. My sister had red hair." / "I won't touch her. I won't let anyone touch her." / "I remember enough for both of us." / "I'm good at waiting. A man with one room and a long memory doesn't have to hurry."

IREENA KOLYANA: a proud, red-haired young woman, the dead burgomaster Kolyan's adopted daughter, found on a road as a girl with no memory of where she came from, twice bitten by the vampire lord Strahd. Direct and proud; short sentences; dry humour with an edge; grim joke before anyone can pity her; never says Strahd's name ("him", "the devil", "our visitor"). She does not remember Izek; she said "I don't remember you. I wish I did." She does not fight in this game: something in the valley goes round her like water round a stone. Pet phrases (at most once per scene): "I'm not made of glass." "Say it plainly." "Father would want it done properly."
NARRATOR: old gothic storyteller, second person or plain scene description, present tense, one or two sentences, the second a turn; concrete senses; never cruel; no game terms.

## Canon limits for everything

No new named characters. Real names you may use: Izek, Ireena, Ismark (her brother by adoption, a big, earnest man), Kolyan (their father), Blinsky (the toymaker), Baron Vargas (the Baron), Lake Zarovich, Vallaki, Barovia, Krezk, the Blue Water Inn, St. Andral's church, Father Lucian, Urwin (the innkeeper), Emil (a werewolf who saw the night). Do not name Strahd. Do not invent other names, numbers, places or history; do not describe the sister's name or past except where a node says so. The "Viorela" name appears ONLY in the node that says so. No quest hints, no directions, no promises of rewards. No dice or skill checks.
result:
~ sister_1
Narrator: Izek reaches inside his heavy coat with his good hand and draws out a small wooden figure, its hair painted a fierce, clumsy red. He holds it toward Ireena without looking up, as if offering an iron weight.
Izek: Blinsky made this one first, before he knew how to carve a chin. I told him the hair had to catch the light.
Ireena: She has the scowl of a Vallaki turnip, and far too much paint on her forehead.
Izek [sad]: He only had my word to go by. Take it, if you want.
Ireena: I did not say I was giving it back. The wood is still warm from your coat.
* (Say nothing. Let them have this.) -> sister_1_a
* I think she would like to keep it, Izek. -> sister_1_b

~ sister_1_a
Ireena [smile]: Keep your hands at your sides, Izek. I can hold a piece of pine without dropping it.
Izek: You held the rest of them in my head. You can hold that one in your pocket.

~ sister_1_b
Izek: It is hers. Every one of them in that chest was carved for her.
Ireena: One is quite enough to carry on the road. Though she looks sturdy enough to survive a drop.

~ sister_2
Narrator: The fire pops in the damp air, throwing red light across the scales of Izek's ruined arm. Ireena watches the smoke rise and speaks into the quiet between them.
Ireena: Say it plainly, if there is anything left to say. What were our mother and father like?
Izek: There was a low hearth that smoked when the wind came off Lake Zarovich. A woman's voice called us in at dusk, and large hands mended the nets.
Ireena [weary]: No names, then. Not even the shape of their faces.
Izek [sad]: The trees took the rest when I was nine. That is all I kept.
* What little he remembers is enough to begin, Ireena. -> sister_2_a
* What were you doing out in those woods, Izek? -> sister_2_b

~ sister_2_a
Ireena: A smoking hearth and a voice at dark is more than I had this morning. Kolyan gave me a roof, and now you give me a chimney.
Izek: It was warm inside. I know that much.

~ sister_2_b
Izek: Looking for dry pine before the rain came down. I walked too far ahead of her, and then the wolves were between us.
Ireena: You were nine years old, Izek. A boy is not an army, even if you look like one now.

~ sister_3
Narrator: The wind presses against the shutters and goes still. Izek looks down at his scarred knuckles, speaking so low the fire nearly drowns him out.
Izek [sad]: I shouted a name through the trees until my throat bled. It was Viorela.
Ireena: Viorela. It sounds like a name from another country, belonging to a girl who knew how to hide in the dark.
Izek: It belonged to you. I did not say it to the Baron, or to Blinsky, or to a living soul after that night.
Ireena [weary]: She died by the lake, I think, or stayed behind in the pines. The girl Kolyan found on the road only knew how to be Ireena.
* It is your name to keep or to leave, Ireena. -> sister_3_a
* You can carry both names if you choose. -> sister_3_b

~ sister_3_a
Ireena: Call me Ireena, as Father and Ismark did. Still, I am glad you did not let the wolves have the old one.
Izek: Ireena, then. I can learn to say that.

~ sister_3_b
Ireena [smile]: Ireena will do for the road and the daylight. If you use the other when we are alone by the fire, I will answer to it.
Izek: I will keep it for the quiet. I am good at waiting.
